title: How Flight Attendants Work
summary: Josh and Chuck explore the work of flight attendants: a new Delta safety instruction about lost devices in seats, post-9/11 changes in air travel and security, the decline of flying as a luxury event, and the history of flight attendants from the early cabin boys and Heinrich Kubis (Zeppelin steward) to Ellen Church's 1930 hiring of eight nurses at Boeing Air Transport. They cover the sexist "stewardess" era with weight, height, age and marriage restrictions and airline ads, the intense seven-to-twelve-week training (written and practical tests, emergency drills, Barbie boot camp), human trafficking detection training sparked by flight attendant Sandra Fierini, pay structure (flight-time-only pay, boarding time largely unpaid), buddy passes, and tipping. The episode closes with listener mail from Courtney Harmouth about surviving swine flu as a teenager and the importance of flu vaccination.

segments.title: Lost devices in seats and passenger attitudes toward flight attendants
segments.summary: The hosts open with Delta's new safety instruction not to adjust seats if a phone or tablet is lost in them, then discuss how mean passengers treat flight attendants and how post-9/11 security has made flying more stressful.

segments.title: Shoes, laptops, and the changing experience of flying
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck talk about removing shoes at security, the feel of modern travel versus the past, falling ticket prices, and the lost luxury of 1960s flying with carving stations and piano lounges.

segments.title: Early flight attendants and Ellen Church
segments.summary: The hosts trace the history of flight attendants from early cabin boys and Heinrich Kubis, who worked Zeppelins including the Hindenburg, to Ellen Church, a nurse and pilot who in 1930 persuaded Boeing Air Transport to hire eight women.

segments.title: The sexy stewardess era and airline sexism
segments.summary: The hosts describe the 1950s-1970s stewardess era, with weight and height limits, age cutoffs around 32, marriage and children restrictions, and airline print ads that sold flight attendants as a draw, along with union opposition.

segments.title: Flight attendant hiring and training
segments.summary: Hiring requirements are discussed, including the competitiveness of the job. Training averages seven weeks (up to twelve), with six-day, twelve-hour days, written tests requiring a high score, practical emergency drills, and a focus on safety equipment over customer service.

segments.title: Annual training, sabotage of safety, and onboard responsibilities
segments.summary: The hosts note that flight attendants retrain annually and on new aircraft, discuss passengers who overfill overhead bins, and describe how flight attendants handle drunk passengers and long schedules.

segments.title: Human trafficking detection and the Super Bowl
segments.summary: Flight attendants are trained to spot human trafficking. The hosts describe Sandra Fierini's discovery of an infant with an umbilical cord on a flight, her work with Deborah Sigmund of Innocence at Risk, and flight attendant volunteering at a Super Bowl.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break before the pay discussion.

segments.title: Flight attendant pay, seniority, and unpaid boarding time
segments.summary: The hosts discuss median pay, seniority-based earnings, soap opera actress Kate Linder's flight attending career, and the fact that flight attendants are paid only for flight time, not for boarding, with a small rate for pre-boarding work.

segments.title: Tipping, buddy passes, and notable flight attendant stories
segments.summary: The hosts joke about tipping flight attendants, discuss buddy passes and their drawbacks, and recount Nellie Granger's rescue work after a TWA crash, plus stories of dead bodies being transported on flights.
topics: D.B. Cooper flight attendant Tina Muckler

segments.title: Listener mail: swine flu story
segments.summary: Listener Courtney Harmouth describes being hospitalized with swine flu and pneumonia as a teenager and urges people to get vaccinated against the flu.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts invite listeners to share stories and contact the show.
